The words

How blest the righteous are
When they resign their breath!
No wonder Balaam wished to share
In such a happy death.

"Oh! let me die, said he,
The death the righteous do;
When life is ended let me be
Found with the faithful few."

The force of truth how great!
When enemies confess,
None but the righteous whom they hate,
A solid hope possess.

But Balaam's wish was vain,
His heart was insincere;
He thirsted for unrighteous gain,
And sought a portion here.

He seemed the Lord to know,
And to offend him loth;
But Mammon proved his overthrow,
For none can serve them both.

May you, my friends, and I,
Warning from hence receive;
If like the righteous we would die,
To choose the life they live.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Bb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on l, (G), on the word “How”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 20, “Balaam's wish Num 23:10”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words: John Newton (1725–1807)
  • Music (1762): Samuel Howard (died undefined)

Questions about How Blest the Righteous Are

What is the doh of How Blest the Righteous Are?

In this version, in G minor, doh is Bb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does How Blest the Righteous Are start on?

It starts on l, (G in G minor), a pickup on the word “How” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to l,.

Is How Blest the Righteous Are in the public domain?

Yes. John Newton died in 1807, Samuel Howard died in undefined; the words were in print by 1779 and the music in 1762. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
